annotations.text: J — Numbered Spec Index: a clay 01–12 numeral gutter and 1px hairlines carry the table, with no card, zebra or outer border at any width. Trade-off: the numerals add noise a two-way comparison does not need and can read as a checklist, and the Mobile stack must repeat both column names on every line, which puts it at 2,313px against K's 1,974px.

K — Menu Leaders: dot leaders run from each trait to values right-aligned on a common axis, one leader run per value column, giving the shortest Cvt Mobile stack of any round at 1,974px. Trade-off: the leaders are fragile — 'Roys · Amie · Bery · Jins/Jeni' already squeezes its dot run to the 18px minimum at Tablet, so any longer value would wrap and orphan the run.

J — Numbered Spec Index. A clay numeral gutter plus hairlines carry the whole structure, so nothing boxed can break at 390 / 768 / 1440. Trade-off: numbering a four-row comparison 01-04 reads as a checklist rather than a comparison, and the numerals add visual noise this table does not strictly need.

K — Menu Leaders. Dot leaders run to a common right axis and cut the Mobile stack to 1,417px, the shortest Mvf artboard of any round. Trade-off: the cells here are sentence-length prose, so the axis holds only the value's key; the prose itself breaks to its own line beneath the leader run, and the label column is pinned (240 / 176px) to stop the runs collapsing.

J (Numbered Spec Index): a clay numeral gutter indexes the four species 01 to 04 over hairlines with no boxes or zebra, so the African Grey lead row is carried by type weight and a small-caps label alone; the trade-off is that numbering species reads as a ranked checklist rather than a comparison, and it is the taller Mobile stack of the pair at 1,619px.

K (Menu Leaders): dot leaders run from each species to its three attributes with values right-aligned on a common axis, folding Noise level and Best for into one muted meta line at Tablet; the trade-off is that the sentence-length Best for cells wrap right-aligned and squeeze the leader run down to a stub on the African Grey row.

J — Numbered Spec Index. Trade-off: the 01-06 clay numeral gutter gives the six price tiers an editorial catalogue rhythm with no cards, no zebra and price alone in the heaviest terminal column, but numbering a price list implies a ranked order the six tiers do not actually have, and the gutter costs 64px of column width the Best fit / lifestyle cell would rather use.

K — Menu Leaders. Trade-off: the leader run from subspecies straight to the right-aligned price puts money on a single scan axis and gives the shortest Mobile stack of the two (1,305px vs 1,455px), but the dots are fragile: the longest values sit only about 40px clear of the label at Desktop, so any future price tier with a longer Best fit / lifestyle string wraps and orphans its leader run.
